newsitem.title: USA: Weather speeds South Dakota wheat planting efforts.
newsitem.headline: Weather speeds South Dakota wheat planting efforts.

text.p: Dry weather allowed winter wheat seeding and row crop harvesting to resume in South Dakota during the week ended Sunday, according to the weekly crop report from the state's agricultural statistics service.
"Warm, dry weather improved field conditions after two weeks of rain had halted field work," according to the report.
Winter wheat was 72 percent seeded, against the five-year average of 94 percent. The crop was 48 percent emerged.
Corn was six percent harvested, compared to the five-year average of 16 percent. The corn crop was rated three percent poor, 16 percent fair, 57 percent good and 24 percent excellent.
Soybeans were rated three percent poor, 16 percent fair, 65 percent good and 16 percent excellent. Thirteen percent was harvested, against 32 percent average.
Topsoil moisture was rated nil very short, two percent short, 85 percent adequate and 13 percent surplus.
Pasture and range were rated one percent very poor, six percent poor, 25 percent fair, 56 percent good and 12 percent excellent.
